'''Yarna d'al' Gargan''' was a longtime [[Askajian/Legends|Askajian]] dancer from [[Askaji/Legends|Askaj]] at [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]]. She was present during the presentation of the [[Max Rebo Band/Legends|Max Rebo Band]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
Yarna d'al' Gargan was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Askajian/Legends|Askajian]] who had a [[Gargan family|family]] on her [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], [[Askaji/Legends|Askaj]]. Her [[Parent/Legends|father]] was a tribal [[Chief/Legends|chief]] and her [[Marriage/Legends|husband]] was [[Nautag d'al' Gargan]]. Yarna and Nautag had many children together. While raising her cubs with Nautag they were taken as [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], and were then bought by [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]].<ref name="SWCE" />

===On Tatooine===
Nautag was killed by [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|Jabba's rancor]] while trying to defend them and her cublings were removed to [[Desilijic Complex/Legends|Jabba's town house]].<ref name="SWCE" /> Although she detested her boss and enslaver, she was nonetheless close friends with some of the various patrons of the [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]].

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], as [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] were brought before Jabba, Yarna flirted with a balding Human male. She later performed a dance with [[Oola/Legends|Oola]] prior to the Twi'lek's demise.<ref name="RotJ" />

===Later life===
Yarna decided to honor two of the beings responsible for her freedom by naming her two daughters [[Luka d'al' Gargan|Luka]] and [[Leia d'al' Gargan|Leia]] after [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and Leia Organa; she named her son [[Nautag d'al' Gargan II|Nautag]] after his late father.<ref name="SD" />

After escaping Jabba's palace and rescuing her cubs with the assistance of [[Doallyn/Legends|Doallyn]], they became traders in jewels and textiles. She occasionally danced to earn extra [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] and performed the [[Dance of the Seventy Violet Veils]] at the [[Wedding of Han Solo and Leia Organa/Legends|wedding]] of [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]. At the event, she was spotted by a [[Clothing/Legends|lingerie]] designer and became the model for his jeweled brassieres, with Doallyn managing her modeling career. Yarna's children became a [[Jizz/Legends|jizz]] swing band, and together they toured [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="WBO">{{StoryCite|story=Epilogue: Whatever Became Of...?|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
Her beauty was often hidden by the wart makeup Jabba forced her to wear, saying that it reminded him of his mother<ref name="SWCE" /> and sole parent, [[Zorba Desilijic Tiure]].<ref name="EGC" /> The normally slender woman was made to store as much [[Water/Legends|water]] as possible in order to increase her girth, thus furthering the resemblance to a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]<ref name="SWCE" />&mdash;weight she would eventually lose again after Jabba's [[Death/Legends|death]].

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Somewhere along the way, in one of those conversations that was beer-induced, we said, 'Oh, and she has six breasts!' And somehow it was appropriate for Jabba's palace.|Costume designer [[Nilo Rodis-Jamero]]|<ref name="Star Wars Style Part 6: Return of the Jedi">{{InsiderCite|158|Star Wars Style Part 6: Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'' Style Part 6: ''Return of the Jedi''}}</ref>}}
Yarna d'al' Gargan was portrayed by the late [[Claire Davenport]] in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']]. Director [[Richard Marquand]] cast her after having worked with her in [[Wikipedia:Birth of the Beatles|''Birth of the Beatles'']] (1979), a biopic about [[Wikipedia:The Beatles|The Beatles]] that Marquand also directed, in which Davenport played a nude model. Marquand said "I selected the fat lady, because I think fat ladies are wonderful." Marquand said she pictured the character as a quasi-daughter to Jabba the Hutt, adding: "In my mind, she is Jabba's daughter."<ref name="Making">''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]''</ref> During production of ''Return of the Jedi'', her character was known as Wiebba-wiebba.<ref name="Blog">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-mysteries-who-is-wiebba-wiebba|series=Star Wars Mysteries|text=Who is Wiebba-Wiebba?}}</ref> [[Pablo Hidalgo]] detailed this revelation on The Official Star Wars Blog in [[2013]]. [[Leland Chee]] had however previously identified "[[Weeba Weeba]]" as the human Rancor keeper who wears apparel resembling that of [[Nizuc Bek/Legends|Nizuc Bek]] and [[Velken Tezeri/Legends|Velken Tezeri]] but is not conclusively one or the other.<ref name="Holocron">{{Blog|holocron|27/comments|Jabba's Skiff Guards}}</ref>

[[Kenner Products|Kenner]] considered selling an action figure of Gargan for their [[Star Wars: The Power of the Force (1985 toy line)|''Star Wars: The Power of the Force'']] toy line. According to [[Star Wars Insider 92|''Star Wars Insider'' 92]], the figure made to an intermediate prototype stage before [[Lucasfilm]] put a stop to the idea, apparently considering the character unseemly for a children's toy.<ref name="Insider 92">{{InsiderCite|92|The Toys That Never Were}}</ref> She eventually did receive an action figure from [[Hasbro]] in [[2008]], but it did not sell well.
